reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Reopened Maastricht’s current EER credit tables, appendix and route rules, and the official curriculum’s thesis, field and language sections. Reconstructed the annual credit sums from the official components and checked the distinction between a 25 EC route and a 20 EC final project. Returned to the workbook to retest formal prerequisites, changed offerings and actual course contributions before comparing those findings to the frozen output and its reader-facing selections. This was a same-AI pass.
findings: English-taught full-time Maastricht Global Studies starts in September. The 2026–27 regulations list four 30 EC semesters followed by 25 EC Peace & Justice with field study, a 20 EC thesis or alternative final work, and 15 EC 21st Century Learning. The selected route uses the listed Peace & Justice course sequence and interdisciplinary thesis. A 25 EC minor replaces the Peace & Justice content, skills and field study, with a literature exam of up to 12 EC for an approved minor shortfall. The four language classes are 3 EC each. English and native languages are excluded, and the required proficiency must be reached. Appendix 2 explicitly changes GLO2641 to Researching Tolerance & Beliefs, resolving the earlier catalogue title.

Course years follow chronological order under Article 4.2. Tutorials normally require 83 percent attendance and some skills modules require full attendance under Article 4.4. The first four semesters combine two theme courses, two methods courses, two skills courses, a 4 EC project and the language classes. The 20 EC final work spans periods 3 through 5 in Year 3 and overlaps 21st Century Learning in periods 4 and 5. The standard thesis addresses a globalisation-related topic through at least two disciplines.

Only 2026h2 is planned for Research in a Sustainable Delta, and the workbook imposes no prerequisite. Its early placement permits participation in partner-based inquiry alongside introductory climate and sustainability study. Dynamic Earth moves to 2028h2. Earth System Science Tools has Sustainability Essentials I as its prerequisite and does not depend on Dynamic Earth. The closest plan retains its offers and prerequisites.

Sociology, international law, conflict, history and public health contribute directly to the broad global challenges concept. The environment route has sustained science, resource, policy and economics study. Its distinct fifteen-course change each way is driven by this emphasis. Refugee protection and introductory Dutch are bounded overlaps. Maastricht’s longer language and methods sequences and required final work remain separately identifiable.
